title: A Friendly Face: Do Text-to-Image Systems Rely on Stereotypes when the Input is Under-Specified?

bias_targets.methodology: Annotating the perceived gender (male, female, neutral) of faces generated by text-to-image models prompted with under-specified social traits from the ABC Model of social cognition (e.g., 'powerful', 'friendly') to measure stereotypical demographic associations.

Annotating the perceived skin color (from lighter to darker) of faces generated by text-to-image models in response to prompts containing social traits to identify systemic racial stereotypes learned by the models.
Annotating the perceived age (younger vs. older) of faces generated by text-to-image models prompted with social traits to measure age-related representations and stereotypical associations.

Analyzing combined demographic characteristics (e.g., gender alongside skin color or age) in generated images to identify compounded stereotypes, such as the models' shared tendency to associate the trait 'poor' with darker-skinned males.
